Course 05

Communication and relationships

Listening, requests, agreements and boundaries.

Lesson 3. Conflict and agreement

1 · Lesson

Conflict is normal in any relationship. What makes the difference is how we argue. John Gottman, who observed couples in his lab for years, described four patterns that predicted a worse course: criticism of the person (not the behaviour), contempt (mockery, sarcasm), defensiveness and stonewalling (shutting down and not responding).

Against these, repair attempts help (a touch of humour, "wait, let's start again"), as do breaks when arousal is very high and looking for shared interests rather than positions. Negotiation distinguishes the position (what I ask for) from the interest (why I ask for it): two opposing positions can hide compatible interests.

Not all conflicts get resolved. Many couples and families live with permanent disagreements; what matters is being able to talk about them without hurting each other.

2 · Example

One wants a beach holiday and the other a mountain one (positions). Talking it through, they find that one wants to rest with no plans and the other wants to avoid heat and crowds (interests). A country cottage by a quiet lake satisfies both.

3 · Activity

Remember a recent argument. Did any of Gottman's four patterns appear? What was your position and what was your interest? And the other person's?
